decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Transport Note Revision 1:1 (Dated 15/12/2025),Planning Statement,Flood Risk Assessment,Heritage Statement,1785_304_A (Existing & Proposed Site Plans),1785_303_B (Location Plan),1785_310_A1 (Existing Drawings),1785_330 (Proposed Plan),Email from Agent (Dated 15/04/2026),Email from Agent (Dated 17/03/2026).Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Prior to the commencement of any works, the following information shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority:1. A method statement for the careful deconstruction of the building.2. A construction management plan for protecting the front main building, namely the fire station.3. A Written Scheme of Investigation (WSI): A WSI for the recording of the building and its fabric, to include details of the recording methodology, the level of detail to be captured during dismantling, and the qualifications of the specialist undertaking the work. The recording shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved WSI. A copy of the final building recording report shall thereafter be submitted to both GLAAS and the relevant Local Studies Archive.4. Evidence confirming submission of the final building recording report to GLAAS and the relevant Local Studies Archive. The report shall be prepared and presented in accordance with the approved Written Scheme of Investigation and to a standard suitable for long-term public record and research use.The works shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details.Reason: In the interests of proper planning and to preserve local character.

No development shall commence until the drying tower, which lies partly within the application site and immediately to the west of it, has been fully demolished and the site has been cleared of all resulting materials. The drying tower shall be demolished in accordance with an approved demolition method statement.Reason: To ensure the safe removal of the structure and to enable the development to proceed without obstruction.

Prior to the sale of any unit, information boards showcasing the history of the drying tower shall be installed on-site in locations clearly visible to the public. Details of the boards, including their number, design, materials, location, colours, and content, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to installation.Reason: In order to ensure that the historic importance of this building is recognised and to ensure that site history is preserved.

Prior to the commencement of development, a Dust Management Plan (DMP), based on an Air Quality and Dust Risk Assessment (AQDRA), shall be submitted to and approved, in writing, by the local planning authority. The DMP shall be in accordance with The Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG 2014. The DMP will need to detail the measures to reduce the impacts during the construction phase. The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved plan.During each four construction sub-phases of the proposed development (demolition, earthworks, construction, and trackout), PM10 continuous monitoring shall be carried out on site. Parameters to be monitored, duration, locations and monitoring techniques must be approved in writing by the London Borough of Enfield prior to commencement of monitoring.Reason: To protect the local amenity from demolition/construction dust.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2020 (or any regulations revoking or re-enacting these regulations with or without modification),  the use hereby approved is limited to Use Class E(c)(ii) - Professional services (office), with no permitted changes within Class E without the prior written permission of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the character of the area, and residential amenities of nearby residential properties.

No works shall commence on site until a Demolition and Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Demolition and Construction Management Plan shall include: - hours of construction activity- a photographic survey of the existing conditions of adjacent public highways - an assessment of the cumulative impacts of demolition and construction traffic- details of the likely volume of demolition and construction trips and any mitigation measures- site access and exit arrangements including wheel washing facilities and sweep-paths where required- vehicular routes, booking systems and an assessment for the scope of consolidating loads to reduce generated road trips- proposed temporary access and parking suspensions and any temporary access and parking solutions required- site compound arrangements including arrival of vehicles, parking, loading, storage and waste arrangements- methods for of protection of adjacent highway infrastructure - an assessment of all matters as are likely to cause nuisance to adjoining occupiers (including but not limited to; noise, dust, smoke, road cleaning, odour control) accompanied by mitigation measures addressing all matters relevant to this particular site. Works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Demolition and Construction Management Plan.Reason: To ensure that works do not prejudice the ability of neighbouring occupier's reasonable enjoyment of their properties and to ensure that works shall not represent any unacceptable level of vehicle movements such that the safety of pedestrians or other road users shall be unduly prejudiced. The imposition of this prior to commencement planning condition is considered necessary to prevent commencement of works until the requirements have been met because the timing of compliance is fundamental to the decision to grant planning permission.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any Order revoking or re-enacting that Order with or without modification), no development within Schedule 2, Part 3, Class MA shall take place without the prior written permission of the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To safeguard the character of the area, and residential amenities of nearby residential properties, and to ensure that a suitable standard of accommodation is provided.

The office use hereby permitted shall not be occupied outside of the following operation hours unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority:Monday to Friday: 08:00am to 18:00pmSaturday, Sunday and Bank Holidays: 08:00am to 13:00pmReason: To safeguard the character of the area, and residential amenities of nearby residential properties

Notwithstanding the details shown within the submitted drawings and documents, the development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until details of a revised scheme of car parking has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The submitted details shall indicate:-	The provision of a maximum of two on-site car parking spaces.-	The location of proposed car parking.-	The dimensions of car parking spaces.In addition, swept path drawings shall be provided to demonstrate that the proposed parking spaces are large enough to accommodate both vehicles' movements independently, and can be safety accessed. Car parking shall be provided in accordance with the approved details prior to the first occupation of the development, and shall be retained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure that car parking facilities are adequate, and to ensure that proposed car parking does not comprise pedestrian and vehicular safety.

Notwithstanding the details indicated within the submitted Planning Statement, the development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until details on proposed cycle parking have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. A minimum of 1.no long stay cycle parking space shall be provided, and a minimum of 6.no short stay cycle parking spaces shall be provided.The submitted details shall indicate; the total quantum of long and short stay cycle parking spaces to be provided, the location of proposed cycle parking, the design and proportions of any cycle stores, the design and proportions of cycle stands, spacing between cycle stands, and measures of security for proposed cycle storage. Cycle storage shall be provided in full accordance with the approved details prior to the first occupation of the development, and shall be retained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that adequate cycle parking facilities are provided to promote sustainable modes of transport.

Notwithstanding the details indicated within the submitted Planning Statement, the development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until details on waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site, in accordance with Building Regulations and Manual for Streets have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Waste storage and recycling facilities shall be provided in accordance with the approved details prior to the first occupation of the development, and shall be retained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets.
